text: {"kind":"final","content":"{\"answer\":\"Evidence from Root Route: today Halcyon keeps 71.0% on-time (onTime: 0.7099917252792718). Sample: 48,340 deliveries, 14,019 late, penalties of $872,460 and handling cost $476,646; 9 at-risk accounts representing $14,200,000 revenue. 67.3% of late deliveries trace to causes before pickup. The five causes are incomplete address at intake (5,994 deliveries, 64.6% late), same-day order after 8am cut-off (4,826, 61.0% late), shipped from a non-nearest warehouse (6,700, 49.9% late), nearest warehouse out of stock (6,009, 50.0% late), bad carrier lane or Carrier D on a Friday (10,030, 45.4% late). Route overruns (>20% over plan) affect 2,880 deliveries, 62.6% late.\\n\\nReplay evidence: fixing only route overruns raises on-time to 73.6% (lateAvoided: 1,279; costAvoided: $113,347). Fixing carrier lanes plus routes lifts on-time to 80.4% (lateAvoided: 4,523; costAvoided: $409,897). Fixing address + cut-off + stock before pickup raises on-time to 87.8% (lateAvoided: 8,112; costAvoided: $801,412). Fixing everything except route overruns reaches 96.3% on-time (lateAvoided: 12,239; costAvoided: $1,184,850).\\n\\nSuggestion (from the data, not a decision): the data shows routing fixes (carrier lanes + routes) would raise on-time to 80.4%, but addressing pre-pickup causes (address + cut-off + stock) would raise it further to 87.8%; the latter also avoids more late deliveries (8,112 vs 4,523) and more cost ($801,412 vs $409,897). What would change this conclusion is evidence that carrier-lane fixes alone could be implemented at significantly lower operational cost or that routing would be adopted immediately and fully; otherwise, the data points to prioritising pre-pickup fixes alongside any routing pilot. The decision stays with Halcyon.\",\"refused\":false}"}
